messages.author: f7676867a3fe9d9a
messages.subject: error compiling example models
parts:
Hi,

I used to run my models on Stan (RStan) with no problem (it was March).
In September I used the same models, but I got a compiling error and is still there with RStan 2.8
I am running RStan on a i7 4 core, 16 Gb, Debian/GNU Linux machine with g++ v4.9.2. Below are the specification of my system.

I tried to run the models provided as example, but with no success.
These may be the relevant error messages:

/usr/lib/R/etc/Makeconf:143: instruction set for the objective "file4154a74f4b0.o" failed

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) :
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! make: *** [file4154a74f4b0.o] Error 1R version 3.2.2 (2015-08-14)

I attach a log file of the run and my "Makeconf" file.


sessionInfo() output:
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Debian GNU/Linux 8 (jessie)

locale:

other attached packages:
[1] rstan_2.8.0    ggplot2_1.0.1  Rcpp_0.12.1    vimcom_1.2-6   setwidth_1.0-4
[6] colorout_1.0-2

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] digest_0.6.8     MASS_7.3-44      grid_3.2.2       plyr_1.8.3       gtable_0.1.2   
 [6] stats4_3.2.2     magrittr_1.5     scales_0.3.0     stringi_0.5-5    reshape2_1.4.1 
[11] proto_0.3-10     tools_3.2.2      stringr_1.0.0    munsell_0.4.2    parallel_3.2.2 
[16] inline_0.3.14    colorspace_1.2-6 gridExtra_2.0.0


.R/Makevars:
^^^^^^^^^^^^
CXXFLAGS=-O3
CXXFLAGS+=-flto -ffat-lto-objects

To run the models I execute the following commands
(as instructed in the school example:

schools_dat <- list(J = 8,
                    y = c(28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12),
                    sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18))

library(rstan)
# I tried with and without the following two lines (but that does not make any difference):
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

fit <- stan(file = '8schools.stan', data = schools_dat,
            iter = 1000, chains = 4, verbose=TRUE)

The model:
^^^^^^^^^^
The model is the one in the school example:

data {
  int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
  real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
  real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> tau;
  real eta[J];
}
transformed parameters {
  real theta[J];
  for (j in 1:J)
    theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
}
model {
  eta ~ normal(0, 1);
  y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
}


Thanks for any help,

  Davide

messages.author: f7676867a3fe9d9a
messages.subject: Re: error compiling example models
parts: I do not now what was the problem and what changed now, but it is gone. After many unsuccessful attempts I worked on something else. Yesterday I tried again (to work on the problem) without changing anything, and the compilation worked (and so the fit).
